Incorporating the July 2021 Beige Book further brightens the assessment of the July 28, 2021 FOMC statement beyond the SLOOS read. The FOMC remained dovish (policy rate at 0–0.25%, ongoing Treasury and MBS purchases, tolerance for inflation moderately above 2%), signaling easy financial conditions. The July SLOOS corroborated this with stronger demand for C&I loans across firm sizes, easing C&I and consumer credit terms, and firmer QM mortgage demand—evidence that credit supply and demand are supportive.

The Beige Book adds on-the-ground confirmation of strengthening activity:
- Hiring increased across regions, indicating continued labor-market healing.
- Wages moved higher, consistent with tighter labor conditions and firming demand.
- Tourism activity rebounded (notably in the New York area), pointing to service-sector normalization.

These Beige Book signals reinforce growth momentum and complement the SLOOS’s improvement in credit availability. While higher wages can imply some inflation persistence, the FOMC’s stated tolerance for inflation moderately above 2% and commitment to accommodative policy mitigate near-term downside from that risk. Net effect: a modest upgrade to the outlook versus the prior FOMC+SLOOS view.
